Plot vector contours or properties

Source: R/images.R
plot.mlv_drawing.Rd

Draws the drawing on its canvas in image coordinates (x rightward, y downward, equal aspect ratio). The canvas spans the raster extent, 0.5 to `width + 0.5` and 0.5 to `height + 0.5`, because pixel centres lie at integers starting at 1; the plot coordinates are those of [plot.mlv_mat()], so MAT stages and drawings overlay exactly. With a `property`, segments are coloured by that quantity and, by default, a colour bar naming the quantity and its unit is drawn to the right of the canvas, inside the plot region, so later low-level calls (`points()`, `text()`) use the same coordinates. To keep the bar out of the plot region, or to share one bar between panels, draw with `legend = FALSE` and add [colour_key()] in a [graphics::layout()] cell.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mlv_drawing'
plot(
  x,
  property = NULL,
  col = "black",
  lwd = 1,
  ...,
  legend = TRUE,
  palette = NULL,
  zlim = NULL,
  arms = FALSE,
  arm_length = NULL,
  junction_col = "#D55E00",
  frame = TRUE,
  arm_lwd = NULL,
  fan = 0,
  gaps = FALSE,
  reference_junctions = NULL,
  pixel_grid = FALSE,
  reach = NULL,
  reach_epsilon = NULL,
  add = FALSE,
  arm_head = 0.075
)

Arguments

x

A drawing.

property

Optional segment property (`"orientation"`, `"length"`, `"curvature"`), `"junctions"`, or a mapped MAT property.

col

Contour colour when no segment property is shown; one colour, or one per segment. With a mapped medial-axis property it is the colour of the vector contours drawn under the mapped pixels: the default draws them in grey, and `NA` leaves them out.

lwd

Line width.

...

Arguments to the initial plot, such as `main`, `xlim` or `axes = FALSE`.

legend

Draw a colour bar when colour encodes a quantity.

palette

Optional palette: a function of the number of colours, or a character vector of colours. Defaults are described above.

zlim

Value range mapped onto the palette for length and curvature; values outside it take the end colours. Defaults to the finite data range. Ignored for orientation (always 0 to 180 degrees) and MAT scores (0 to 1).

arms

Draw junction arms.

arm_length

Drawn arm length in pixels; defaults to 8 canvas side.

junction_col

Colour of junction markers and arms.

frame

Outline the canvas in light grey.

arm_lwd

Width of the arm bands; defaults to `2.5 * lwd`, at least 3.

fan

Angle in degrees between drawn arms that share an orientation; 0 (default) draws them on one line with stacked arrowheads.

gaps

Draw and label the angular gaps between arms: `TRUE` for every gap (shading the unique largest), `"min"` for the smallest gap only, the one reported as `min_angle`, or `"max"` for the largest gap only, the one that decides between Y, T and Arrow.

reference_junctions

Optional junction table, for example `detect_junctions(x)` under another rule, whose arms are drawn as thin grey dashed arrows beneath the drawn arms for comparison.

pixel_grid

Draw the pixel boundaries in light grey.

reach

`NULL` (default), `"euclidean"` or `"chebyshev"`: draw the gap allowance under that metric at each free contour end.

reach_epsilon

The absolute (pixels) and relative limits of the allowance, as `absolute_epsilon` and `relative_epsilon` of [detect_junctions()]; defaults to that function's defaults.

add

Draw onto the current plot, in its coordinates, instead of starting a new one; no axes, frame or colour bar are drawn. Useful for overlaying a drawing on another, for example a transformed copy on its original.

arm_head

Length of the arrowheads, in inches.

Value

The drawing invisibly.

Details

Orientation is axial: a segment at 10 degrees and one at 190 degrees have the same colour, and the default palette is a cyclic hue wheel over 0 to 180 degrees, so 0 and 180 share a colour. Length and curvature use the sequential Viridis palette over `zlim`. Mapped medial-axis scores are drawn as filled mapped pixels on a 0 to 1 Viridis scale over grey contours.

With `property = "junctions"`, or `arms = TRUE`, junction positions are marked. `arms = TRUE` also draws each arm leaving the junction along its orientation (the `arms` column of [detect_junctions()]): a translucent band drawn beneath the ink, so the contour stays visible along the arm, with an arrowhead at its end. An arm that lies on no ink, which some rules produce, shows as a band without a stroke. Arms that share an orientation are drawn on one line with one arrowhead each, stacked along the arm, and labelled with their count ("x2" drawn with a multiplication sign), so every arm can be counted; `fan` spreads them by an angle instead. `gaps = TRUE` draws each angular gap between consecutive arms as an arc labelled in degrees and shades the largest gap when it is unique, the gap that separates Y, T and Arrow junctions. Junctions come from the drawing's stored `junctions` (for example from [compute_contour_properties()] with `rule = "mlv2023"`), its feature specification, or default [detect_junctions()].

Two options help with pixel-scale views (use `xlim` and `ylim` to zoom): `pixel_grid = TRUE` draws the pixel boundaries, which lie half-way between the integer pixel centres, and `reach` draws the gap allowance of [detect_junctions()] at each free end of an open contour: the set of extension of the end segment along its own line (solid, with a tick at its end) as far as the allowance lets it reach, and, as a dashed grey outline, the set of points within `reach_epsilon[1]` of the end under the chosen metric (a disc for `"euclidean"`, an axis-aligned square for `"chebyshev"`). The extension stops where the segment's line leaves that set, or at `reach_epsilon[2]` of the segment's length when that is stricter. Only the extension decides whether a junction is found: another contour that crosses the outline but not the extension is not met. Along a diagonal the Chebyshev square lets the extension reach `sqrt(2)` times further than the disc.

Examples

d <- mlv_drawing(list(rbind(c(5, 10, 35, 10)), rbind(c(20, 10, 20, 35))), 40, 40)
plot(d, property = "orientation")

plot(d, property = "junctions", arms = TRUE, gaps = TRUE, axes = FALSE)

# A pixel-scale view of a stem that stops 1.3 px short of a bar.
g <- mlv_drawing(list(rbind(c(5, 20, 35, 20)), rbind(c(20, 21.3, 20, 35))), 40, 40)
plot(g, xlim = c(16, 24), ylim = c(25, 17), pixel_grid = TRUE,
     reach = "euclidean", axes = FALSE, frame = FALSE, lwd = 2)

# A rotated copy over its original.
plot(d, col = "grey80", lwd = 2)
plot(rotate_drawing(d, 30), add = TRUE, lwd = 2)
